title: Mosaic clone notation
clinical_history: Two cell lines are written in one ISCN string. Read the slash and the numbers in square brackets. This exercise teaches the notation. It does not assign a syndrome.
plain_language_interpretation: Two cell lines: 6 cells have an extra chromosome 8, and 14 cells are 46,XX. A slash separates cell lines. Numbers in square brackets are cell counts, not chromosome counts. No syndrome is assigned here.
explanation: ISCN writes more than one cell line with a slash. The number in square brackets is how many cells were counted in that line. 47,XX,+8[6]/46,XX[14] means six cells with an extra chromosome 8 and fourteen cells with a normal female complement. The exercise stops at that reading.
hints: A slash in ISCN separates cell lines, not chromosomes.
The number in square brackets is the number of cells in that line, not the chromosome count.
The first line has 47 chromosomes because one chromosome 8 is extra. The second line is 46,XX.
